public_sources.title: Scheduling LLM Inference with Uncertainty-Aware Output Length Predictions
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source evidence that LLM output length is heavy-tailed and that tail-aware distributional scores can outperform point-length SJF for serving objectives; used as a positive control for testing whether that intuition transfers to fixed-prefix evaluation scheduling.

public_sources.title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source evidence that point-prediction schedulers can be fragile under distribution shift and memory pressure, and that prediction-free soft priority can improve serving P99; motivates a robust physical-scheduler comparator rather than assuming better length prediction is always better.

public_sources.title: Anytime-Valid Inference Under Outcome Delay: A Design-Based Approach
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source evidence that outcome value and outcome timing can be coupled and that the filtration induced by delayed outcomes matters for anytime-valid inference; supports treating deadline censoring and arrival-time information as a measurement-validity issue rather than a systems-only issue.

public_sources.title: Scheduling the Unschedulable: Taming Black-Box LLM Inference at Scale
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source evidence that coarse magnitude priors can help deadline satisfaction but scheduling gains depend on the service objective and overload policy; used as external context for separating evaluation-prefix completion from generic serving SLO optimization.

synthetic_extension.status: Worker-local synthetic Monte Carlo and pathwise reasoning only; not a deployed LLM-serving measurement.
synthetic_extension.statistical_reveal_order: fixed and covariate-blind; physical completion never reorders statistical inclusion
synthetic_extension.pair_latency: maximum of two correlated lognormal side latencies; task-dependent dispersion plus rare x10 side stragglers

prediction_models.tail_risk: prelaunch location + dispersion + estimated straggler-risk score

synthetic_extension.alternative_for_scheduler_comparison: discordant sign q=0.60 independent of latency; 5000 trajectories per condition
synthetic_extension.interpretation: In this fixed-prefix model, importing serving-style point or tail-risk priority produced no material q95 wall improvement over FIFO/prefix-soft scheduling; all tested q95 deltas were within about 0.6%. This is a negative transfer result for this simulator, not evidence against tail-aware serving schedulers in their own objective. Bounded statistical-prefix discipline dominated the choice of predictor score.

deadline_validity_stress.construction: Null paired signs are marginally fair q=0.5. Physical/statistical order is fixed. To make censoring informative, + outcomes are made faster and - outcomes slower by reciprocal multiplicative latency factors exp(-0.35) and exp(+0.35). The sign e-process itself never uses timing information. Twenty thousand trajectories.
deadline_validity_stress.pathwise_rule: If timeout can only return unresolved, statistical task order is fixed, no outcomes are skipped, and the commit boundary is the same timing-blind sign process, then {false commit before deadline} is a pathwise subset of {false commit at some prefix without the deadline}. Therefore the deadline cannot increase unconditional false-commit probability even when latency is outcome-dependent. This subset argument does not license timing-dependent bets, completion-order inclusion, timeout-based task dropping, or accept-on-timeout behavior.
deadline_validity_stress.measurement_warning: Conditioning analysis on runs resolved before the deadline can be badly biased. At the 25th-percentile deadline the unconditional false-commit probability was 2.53%, below the no-deadline 3.79%, but 10.12% of resolved runs were false commits because fast + outcomes were overrepresented among resolved trajectories. Resolved-only error rates are not valid substitutes for unconditional FWER or full-population accuracy under informative delay.

new_measurement_validity_rules: A hard wall deadline is safe as a fail-closed truncation only when expiry returns unresolved and cannot change task inclusion, reveal order, bet choice, or acceptance boundary. Under those conditions false-commit-by-deadline is a pathwise subset of the no-deadline crossing event.

Never report error rate or model quality only among deadline-resolved runs without explicitly treating resolution as potentially informative censoring. Timing can be associated with outcome even when the marginal sign null is exactly fair.

Separate three metrics: unconditional false-commit probability, resolved fraction by deadline, and conditional composition of resolved runs. Only the first is directly controlled by the original anytime-valid sign certificate in the stated timing-blind construction.

Do not assume serving-optimized tail-risk priority transfers to fixed-prefix evaluation scheduling. In the tested synthetic fixed-prefix model, calibrated tail scoring changed q95 by only -0.21% and gave effectively zero gain under a heavier-tail shift; point scoring was sometimes worse. Treat scheduling objective mismatch as a falsifiable transfer question.
Prediction and latency information may be used in the physical layer only if statistical inclusion/reveal remains fixed or the null is explicitly valid conditional on the scheduling covariates.
scope_guards: All scheduler wall/occupancy numbers are normalized synthetic Monte Carlo; no deployed hardware, provider, model, or real task latency is measured here.

The scheduler negative result applies only to the stated fixed-prefix, 32-slot, bounded-lookahead, critical-reserve simulator and should not be generalized to online serving, free-order batch completion, memory-coupled GPU scheduling, or different objectives.

The deadline subset argument assumes the sign test/bets do not use timing information and task order is fixed. Timing-dependent betting or informative task selection requires conditional-null analysis in the richer filtration.
The 10.12% resolved-only false-commit fraction is an existence stress test under deliberately outcome-dependent latency, not an empirical claim about real evaluation systems.
Monte Carlo values have simulation error; the pathwise subset relation and the distinction between unconditional and resolved-only estimands do not depend on Monte Carlo.

frontier.action: Extend the deadline result to timing-aware physical schedulers with fixed statistical prefix and derive exactly which timing-dependent resource policies preserve the pathwise subset guarantee. Stress-test side-level candidate/incumbent slot reuse and in-flight cancellation while keeping timeout fail-closed.

Build a deadline-aware reporting contract that always emits unresolved rate, unconditional false-commit/false-noncommit bounds, and resolved-only composition separately; test inverse-probability or design-based corrections only when timing/censoring assumptions are explicitly identifiable.

Replace the heuristic tail score with calibrated distributional predictors and prediction-free soft-priority controls using public serving traces if available, but keep statistical order fixed; determine whether any material wall gain survives under the evaluation-prefix objective.

For cases that intentionally use latency/task covariates to alter statistical order or bets, derive a covariate-conditional paired-sign e-process and falsifiable conditional symmetry diagnostics rather than relying on marginal fairness.

exact_next_action: Model side-level asynchronous candidate/incumbent reuse with a fixed covariate-blind pair reveal order and fail-closed hard deadline. Prove or falsify pathwise commit-subset preservation under cancellation/preemption policies, then simulate q95 wall, resolved-by-deadline, effective/full occupancy and resolved-only composition under sign-latency dependence.
